cards.power: Paranoia. +1 Defense, -5 Chill.
cards.lore: 11,000 years ago, someone looked at their house and immediately thought about how to stop other people from taking it.
cards.gradeReason: 11,000 years of paranoia in one sentence — embody the original fence-builder instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ancient carved relief. Subject: paranoid stone-cutter stacking rocks at dawn. Mood: primal anxiety.

cards.power: Thirst Trap. If you forgot to enclose the well, the siege is already over.
cards.lore: The city that builds walls without water inside has solved invasion but created a death sentence.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp defensive lesson — tells you what to know, not quite what to become.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval manuscript marginalia. Subject: empty stone well surrounded by besieging army. Mood: grim irony.

cards.power: High Ground Fail. Enemy gains +2 Gravity Advantage.
cards.lore: Never build next to the enemy's hill. They will stand on it and mock you.
cards.gradeReason: The mockery is implied but you need context to fully inhabit the loser king.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: comedic sketch. Subject: castle perched below enemy hill, boulders falling, goats watching. Mood: slapstick defeat.

cards.power: Budget Cut. Swap Height for Length. You cannot have both.
cards.lore: The perfect wall does not exist. The enemy will find the cheap section.
cards.gradeReason: Clean impossible-choice lesson, but more advisor than performer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: blueprint engineering diagram. Subject: impossibly long thin wall vs. tiny impenetrable fortress. Mood: bureaucratic despair.

cards.power: Extreme Patience. Force a stalemate until everyone forgets why they are fighting.
cards.lore: The benchmark for stubbornness. If you haven't waited a decade, are you even trying?
cards.gradeReason: Force a stalemate until everyone forgets why — stubbornness role lands without delay.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: classical Greek fresco. Subject: soldiers playing dice outside city walls, calendar showing years passed. Mood: bored determination.

cards.power: The Bamboozle. Bypasses all physical defense via psychological hack.
cards.lore: Not a military tactic. A piece of theater so audacious nobody checked the trunk.
cards.gradeReason: Theater over tactics — nobody checked the trunk. You are the performance, not the weapon.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: theatrical poster. Subject: giant hollow horse on wheels outside Troy gates, gift bow attached. Mood: audacious con.

cards.power: Doom Scroll. You are 100% correct, but nobody listens.
cards.lore: Cursed with accurate data and zero engagement metrics.
cards.gradeReason: 100% correct, zero engagement metrics — the curse is instantly wearable as a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: owl shouting DOOM into megaphone while crowd checks TikTok. Mood: vindicated despair.

cards.power: Weaponized Generosity. Timeo Danaos et dona ferentes.
cards.lore: The most dangerous thing in a siege is a free lunch.
cards.gradeReason: Timeo Danaos — the free lunch danger is immediate. Play the generous enemy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Greek amphora painting. Subject: enormous gift box with hidden soldiers, recipients smiling nervously. Mood: weaponized generosity.

cards.power: Headache. Apply concentrated force until the problem goes away.
cards.lore: Named after the animal that solves problems by hitting them with its forehead.
cards.gradeReason: Named after an animal that headbutts problems — embody the creature, instant comedy role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Roman relief carving. Subject: rhinos carrying a ram-headed log toward fortress gates. Mood: focused brutality.

cards.power: Hard Shell. Immunity to dropping objects (mostly).
cards.lore: Literal tortoises irritating nature to avoid boiling oil.
cards.gradeReason: Hard Shell works, but tortoise formation needs you to know you're already inside one.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Roman tactical diagram. Subject: soldiers locked under overlapping shields in tortoise formation. Mood: claustrophobic discipline.

cards.power: Horizontal Hate. Sniper damage against soft targets.
cards.lore: The Roman answer to "that guy over there specifically."
cards.gradeReason: Sniper hate for that guy over there — needs a specific target to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Roman technical drawing. Subject: giant crossbow aimed at single specific target in crowd. Mood: precise malice.

cards.power: The Lob. Kata-palein (to hurl down). Ignores walls by going over them.
cards.lore: When you can't go through, go over.
cards.gradeReason: Clean tactical logic — more problem-solving frame than embodied performer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval siege manual illustration. Subject: catapult hurling boulder over castle wall, squirrel watching. Mood: elegant overkill.

cards.power: Superior Engine. Uses Gravity, not tension. Hits harder, throws further.
cards.lore: The physics of 'Ouch.' Converts potential energy into a very bad day for the wall.
cards.gradeReason: Superior engine, gravity not tension — the physics impress but the role needs more than specs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: physics textbook illustration. Subject: massive trebuchet counterweight dropping, stone flying toward castle. Mood: elegant destruction.

cards.power: Gravity's Hammer. The heavier the box, the bigger the smash.
cards.lore: Replaced the muscle power of the crew with the constant pull of the planet.
cards.gradeReason: Replaced muscle with planet — smart engineering story, but mechanical not embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: engineering blueprint. Subject: massive weighted box pulling trebuchet arm down, rocks queued below. Mood: mechanical inevitability.

cards.power: Liquid Nightmare. Burns on water. Cannot be extinguished.
cards.lore: The formula is lost, but the screaming remains. Naphtha? Quicklime? Magic?
cards.gradeReason: Formula lost, screaming remains — visceral and immediate. The Liquid Nightmare plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: alchemical manuscript. Subject: green flames burning on water surface, soldiers fleeing burning ships. Mood: apocalyptic mystery.

cards.power: Byzantine BBQ. Psychological terror + fire damage.
cards.lore: Ancient technology that shouldn't exist but definitely did.
cards.gradeReason: Shouldn't exist but did — compelling history, more lecture than performance trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Byzantine mosaic. Subject: fox-headed warrior on ship spraying fire from bronze tube. Mood: anachronistic dread.

cards.power: The Hug. Passive compression. No one gets out.
cards.lore: To build a wall around a wall is to say: "We aren't attacking, we're waiting."
cards.gradeReason: We aren't attacking, we're waiting — the patient siege posture is immediately performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: aerial map illustration. Subject: concentric rings of walls, inner city trapped, outer army waiting. Mood: patient suffocation.

cards.power: Double Trouble. Defend against the city AND the rescue party.
cards.lore: Being besieged while you are besieging. The Caesar Special.
cards.gradeReason: Caesar Special is evocative but the double-siege sandwich needs context before playing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: military campaign map. Subject: Caesar's siege lines facing both city and incoming relief army. Mood: strategic overextension.

cards.power: Undermine. Attacks the foundation, not the face.
cards.lore: Dig a hole, support with wood, burn the wood, watch the wall vanish.
cards.gradeReason: Sequential steps — dig, support, burn, vanish — make it process-heavy over performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cross-section architectural diagram. Subject: tunnel under castle wall with burning wooden supports. Mood: calculated demolition.

cards.power: Tunnel Brawl. Intercept the diggers AND the boom.
cards.lore: Knife fighting in the dark in a space the size of a coffin.
cards.gradeReason: Knife fighting in the dark in a coffin-sized space — visceral, immediate, no context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tight ink sketch. Subject: two groups fighting by candlelight in coffin-sized tunnel underground. Mood: claustrophobic desperation.

cards.power: Calorie Count. Mathematical starvation.
cards.lore: Divide the food by the mouths. If the result is zero, you lose.
cards.gradeReason: Divide food by mouths — if zero, you lose. Clean math but needs numbers to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: monochrome arithmetic diagram. Subject: starving rat guarding single pea on empty plate. Mood: mathematical despair.

cards.power: Inventory. Humans are now just resource consumers.
cards.lore: The first act of defense is accounting.
cards.gradeReason: Humans are now resource consumers — the dehumanizing ledger role activates on contact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic ledger illustration. Subject: owl with clipboard counting exhausted civilians as inventory items. Mood: dehumanized accounting.

cards.power: Moral Crisis. Sacrifice hearts to save stomachs.
cards.lore: Useless mouths are expelled. The besieger won't feed them either.
cards.gradeReason: Useless mouths expelled — besieger won't feed them either. The moral catastrophe is embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval chronicle illustration. Subject: civilians expelled from gate into no-man's land, both gates closing. Mood: moral catastrophe.

cards.power: Game Over. Biology wins.
cards.lore: The arithmetic of defeat. Walls don't matter if you can't lift your sword.
cards.gradeReason: Biology wins, walls useless if you can't lift your sword — the endpoint arrives immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark still life. Subject: massive empty stone granary with cobwebs, single dropped grain on floor. Mood: arithmetic of defeat.

cards.power: The Scald. Budget defense. Free and painful.
cards.lore: Oil is expensive. Water hurts just fine and you can drink the leftovers.
cards.gradeReason: Water hurts fine and you drink the leftovers — budget savagery with immediate dark comedy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: comedic woodcut. Subject: defender pouring cauldron of water while sipping leftovers smugly. Mood: practical brutality.

cards.power: Armor Melter. Bypasses plate defense.
cards.lore: Sand gets inside the suit and cooks you like a baked potato.
cards.gradeReason: Gets inside the suit and cooks you like a baked potato — armored torture, immediately felt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: thermal illustration. Subject: armor suit glowing red from inside, sand pouring from every joint. Mood: internal combustion.

cards.power: Chemical Burn. Reacts with sweat to dissolve faces.
cards.lore: The nastiest dust in history. Do not inhale.
cards.gradeReason: Nastiest dust in history — compelling but you need to know what quicklime does to play it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: hazmat warning diagram. Subject: cloud of white dust dissolving faces of approaching soldiers. Mood: chemical nightmare.

cards.power: Gravity Assist. Recycling your own architecture as ammo.
cards.lore: When out of weapons, throw the castle itself.
cards.gradeReason: Throw the castle itself — clever framing but the recycling logic needs a beat to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: physics trajectory diagram. Subject: castle battlement crumbling, stones redirected as projectiles downward. Mood: architectural recycling.

cards.power: Solid Cover. The bit you stand behind.
cards.lore: Not the gap. The rock. Know the difference or die.
cards.gradeReason: Not the gap. The rock. Know the difference or die — binary, visceral, instantly played.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: minimalist diagram. Subject: duck sheltering behind battlement tooth, arrow flies harmlessly past the gap. Mood: life-or-death geometry.

cards.power: Firing Arc. The bit you shoot through.
cards.lore: Designed to maximize your view and minimize your death.
cards.gradeReason: Describes the slot correctly but technically — explains geometry rather than inviting you to inhabit it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: architectural cross-section. Subject: arrow slit with maximized field of view, minimized exposure angle. Mood: geometric precision.

cards.power: One-Way Mirror. I see you. You can't hit me.
cards.lore: The invisible death slit. Vertical for bows, cross-shaped for crossbows.
cards.gradeReason: I see you. You can't hit me. The one-way mirror role plays without any setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: point-of-view thriller. Subject: eyes watching through narrow slit at incoming army massing below. Mood: invisible dominance.

cards.power: The Drop. Ceiling trap for unwanted guests.
cards.lore: The doorbell that answers with a rock.
cards.gradeReason: The doorbell that answers with a rock — perfect one-liner, the role is instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark comedy ceiling view. Subject: rocks and boiling liquid falling through ceiling hole onto armored guests. Mood: lethal hospitality.

cards.power: Panic Room. The last resort.
cards.lore: Where the VIPs hide when the walls fail. It has its own water.
cards.gradeReason: Panic room of last resort — the refuge role is clear but requires the outer walls failing first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: castle cross-section. Subject: VIPs hiding in inner tower with private water supply, outer walls burning. Mood: elite survival.

cards.power: Eye in the Sky. +10 Perception Range.
cards.lore: Seeing the enemy camp layout before they even unpack.
cards.gradeReason: +10 Perception Range — good intel role but surveillance needs context before performing it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: intelligence report illustration. Subject: crow with telescope watching enemy camp from high tower. Mood: tactical superiority.

cards.power: Rolling Condo. Inverts height advantage.
cards.lore: A moving apartment complex of doom. Requires a very flat road.
cards.gradeReason: Moving apartment complex of doom — the logistics humor is great but the role needs staging.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: engineering nightmare sketch. Subject: massive rolling wooden tower on wheels approaching castle on flat terrain. Mood: lumbering menace.

cards.power: Bridge Drop. The bell tolls for thee.
cards.lore: When this touches your wall, the siege becomes a melee.
cards.gradeReason: Bell tolls for thee — evocative but the bridge-drop mechanism needs a beat before performing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic close-up. Subject: wooden tower making contact with wall, drawbridge dropping into chaos below. Mood: violent threshold.

cards.power: Bio-Ammo. Caffa 1346 Style.
cards.lore: The Mongols catapulted the Black Death into Europe. Tactical and accidental apocalypse.
cards.gradeReason: Bio-Ammo, Caffa 1346, accidental apocalypse — horror and tactic arrive simultaneously.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval horror illustration. Subject: catapult launching wrapped corpse over city walls, crowd fleeing below. Mood: bio-horror comedy.

cards.power: Camp Killer. The army dies from its own waste.
cards.lore: Stationary armies destroy their own environment. The water is now poison.
cards.gradeReason: Camp Killer — clear self-defeat logic but you need to be at the camp to fully feel it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark medical diagram. Subject: army camp with all soldiers queuing for latrine, river water contaminated. Mood: self-inflicted defeat.

cards.power: Bad Command. Politics ruins strategy.
cards.lore: "Attack now, I'm bored." The cause of most failed assaults.
cards.gradeReason: Attack now, I'm bored — the cause of most failed assaults. Character is instantaneous.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: royal portrait parody. Subject: lion king in crown checking hourglass, pointing impatiently at castle. Mood: entitled stupidity.

cards.power: The Survivor. The only true winner of the siege.
cards.lore: While humans starve, the rat thrives.
cards.gradeReason: The only true winner — while humans starve, the rat thrives. Survivor role is instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grim fable illustration. Subject: well-fed rat sitting on pile of defeated human armor. Mood: amoral survival.

cards.power: Immunity. Do not shoot the messenger.
cards.lore: Killing him deletes your WiFi. A universal protocol of war.
cards.gradeReason: Killing him deletes your WiFi — great analogy but diplomatic immunity needs protocol context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heraldic peacock illustration. Subject: ornate herald with trumpet between two armies, arrows paused mid-flight. Mood: diplomatic immunity.

cards.power: Time Out. Talking while reloading.
cards.lore: Assessing the enemy's morale while pretending to discuss terms.
cards.gradeReason: Talking while reloading — assessing morale while pretending to negotiate. Double game is instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: diplomatic spy thriller. Subject: wolf and sheep clinking wine glasses, each reloading under negotiation table. Mood: mutual deception.

cards.power: Universal Pause. "Can we talk?"
cards.lore: Works because everyone needs it to work eventually.
cards.gradeReason: Works because everyone needs it to work eventually — the universal pause is immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: universal symbol illustration. Subject: white flag emerging from rubble, both sides slowly lowering weapons. Mood: pragmatic relief.

cards.power: Betrayal. Whoops, I lied.
cards.lore: Ethics are optional when the granary is empty.
cards.gradeReason: Ethics optional when granary is empty — betrayal role activates on a single clear condition.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir betrayal scene. Subject: signed treaty being stabbed with dagger, empty granary visible in background. Mood: cold pragmatism.

cards.power: Triple Threat. 1,000 Years of "No."
cards.lore: Depth is defense. You break one wall, there are two more.
cards.gradeReason: 1,000 Years of No — impressive historical lesson but scale makes it descriptive over embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Byzantine mosaic. Subject: triple concentric walls of Constantinople with thousand-year timeline above. Mood: monumental defiance.

cards.power: Naval Denial. No boats allowed.
cards.lore: Physical DRM for the ocean.
cards.gradeReason: Physical DRM for the ocean — three words that explain and perform simultaneously. Peak Kayfabizarro.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: naval engineering diagram. Subject: massive chain stretched across harbor, entire fleet bouncing back. Mood: analog firewall.

cards.power: Wall Breaker. 1453 Edition.
cards.lore: The gun that ended the Middle Ages. Fire, cool for an hour, repeat.
cards.gradeReason: Gun that ended the Middle Ages — historic pivot point but weapon description, not embodied role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval technical illustration. Subject: massive bronze cannon aimed at Theodosian walls, crew covering ears. Mood: technological pivot.

cards.power: Entry Point. The argument is over.
cards.lore: Every wall is a question. Gunpowder was the answer.
cards.gradeReason: Every wall is a question, gunpowder was the answer — the threshold moment is immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gunpowder dawn illustration. Subject: wall collapsing in smoke, wolf with flag charging through the gap. Mood: irreversible threshold.

cards.power: Eagle's Nest. Accessibility: Zero.
cards.lore: Militarily unreachable. Logistically isolated.
cards.gradeReason: Eagle's Nest, accessibility zero — strategically perfect but you need to be there to embody it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: geological survey illustration. Subject: fortress atop sheer mesa, eagles circling, no roads or paths visible. Mood: inaccessible perfection.

cards.power: Terraforming. 3 years of moving dirt.
cards.lore: If you can't climb the wall, raise the ground until you can walk over it.
cards.gradeReason: Raise the ground until you walk over it — terraforming logic is good but process-heavy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: engineering project timeline. Subject: Roman soldiers building massive earthen ramp toward mesa, 3-year marker visible. Mood: grinding determination.

cards.power: Denial. You win nothing.
cards.lore: They built a road for three years to conquer a graveyard.
cards.gradeReason: Road built for three years to conquer a graveyard — metaphor lands but needs the backstory first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pyrrhic landscape painting. Subject: Roman soldiers entering empty Masada, nothing inside but silence and wind. Mood: hollow triumph.

cards.power: Self-Deletion. Choosing the exit.
cards.lore: 960 defenders who refused to give the besieger the satisfaction.
cards.gradeReason: Refused to give the besieger the satisfaction — the act of refusal is immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: memento illustration. Subject: 960 figures facing final doorway, refusing to open it for the enemy. Mood: radical refusal.

cards.power: Ladder Rush. High risk, high casualties.
cards.lore: Suicide by climbing. One man on a ladder vs. the entire garrison.
cards.gradeReason: Suicide by climbing is vivid — but you need to feel the tactical desperation before the ladder goes up.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: casualty report illustration. Subject: single soldier on ladder vs. full garrison, arrows raining from above. Mood: suicidal courage.

cards.power: Meat Grinder. The funnel of death.
cards.lore: Pushing into a gap where the enemy has been waiting for you.
cards.gradeReason: Pushing into a gap where the enemy has been waiting — trap and role arrive simultaneously.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tactical diagram horror. Subject: funnel of troops pushing through narrow breach, enemy waiting on both sides. Mood: geometrically inevitable death.

cards.power: Difficult Terrain. -50% Movement Speed.
cards.lore: The wall is down, but the ground is fighting you.
cards.gradeReason: -50% Movement Speed is fun game logic but still describes an obstacle, not an inhabited role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: game mechanic illustration. Subject: soldiers struggling through debris field, movement arrows showing heavy penalties. Mood: physics betrayal.

cards.power: Backdoor Access. Bypasses all defense.
cards.lore: Walls can be impenetrable to force, but they are permeable to bribery.
cards.gradeReason: Impenetrable to force, permeable to bribery — the turnkey role is instant and universal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark comedy illustration. Subject: cloaked figure accepting gold coin, hand on gate latch in moonlight. Mood: structural bribery.

cards.power: Loot. "Recovery of costs."
cards.lore: If you resist the assault, you pay with your furniture (and your life).
cards.gradeReason: Recovery of costs in quotes — the bureaucratic framing of looting is instantly performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: looting ledger illustration. Subject: soldiers carrying furniture and artwork labeled Recovery of Costs. Mood: sardonic accounting.

cards.power: None. Access Denied.
cards.lore: Mercy is for those who surrender before the ram touches the wall.
cards.gradeReason: Timing-based mercy — the rule is clear but you need to know the ram's position to play it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: judicial stamp illustration. Subject: REJECTED stamp on mercy petition, battering ram visible at gate behind. Mood: timing-based justice.

cards.power: New Game. Try again.
cards.lore: The answer to "The wall failed" is always "Build a better wall."
cards.gradeReason: Build a better wall — clean architect's mantra but a lesson, not a player role invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: architectural iteration diagram. Subject: successive wall designs annotated with lessons, newest under construction. Mood: iterative determination.

cards.power: Amnesia. The city forgets what it sits on.
cards.lore: The wall becomes the ground. The ground becomes the city. We forget.
cards.gradeReason: Wall becomes ground, ground becomes city, we forget — the forgetting is performed in reading it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: geological time illustration. Subject: Roman city grown over ancient wall, flowers blooming from former battlements. Mood: melancholy amnesia.

verdict: 60 cards of pure siege-era kayfabe, organized into 15 thematic chapters from Jericho to Masada's last breath. Named strength: 'Physical DRM for the ocean' (The Great Chain) and 'Cursed with accurate data and zero engagement metrics' (Cassandra) are two of the sharpest lore lines in the entire Kayfabizarro corpus — and they're on the same deck. Named weakness: The Embrasure is the lone G3, describing geometry rather than inviting inhabitation — upgrade the lore to 'You are the gap no one sees coming' and it joins the rest. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: From the first paranoid wall at Jericho to Masada's radical refusal, this is humanity's complete guide to violence against architecture — rendered as a card-based comedy for history teachers, improv troupes, and anyone who's ever had to defend a position.

coverQA.coverTitle: 4 — 'Complete Guide to Building Things & Knocking Them Down (Bonus: Greek Fire Recipe Inside!)' is gold; main title slightly long

notes: Structural departure from standard 2x2 card deck: 15 content pages each with a themed chapter header and 4 cards, plus 1 cover page. Cards are cleanly typeset with no decorative font baking artifacts. Each section has its own internal logic arc: Foundations / Troy / Kinetic Weapons / Physics / Mining / Economics / Defensive Nastiness / Architecture / Towers / Biology / Diplomacy / Constantinople / Masada / Assault / Aftermath. Highest G1 concentration in Hot Showers (3/4) and The Waiting Game (3/4). 'Physical DRM for the ocean' (The Great Chain) and 'Cursed with accurate data and zero engagement metrics' (Cassandra) are standout lore lines with crossover viral potential.

quickWins: Upgrade The Embrasure lore to add a performative hook — e.g. 'You are the gap. The archer is your relationship.'
niceToHave: Consider shortening title to 'Kayfabizarro Siege Kompendium' as primary, move subtitle to back cover
The Gift could drop the Latin or add a one-line translation for non-classicists

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: SIEGE KOMPENDIUM – 11,000 Years of Violence Against Architecture (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Nobody ever won a siege by being brave. They won by being patient, well-fed, and willing to catapult a corpse over the wall before breakfast.

A siege is not a battle. It is arithmetic with a body count. You wall off a city, you poison its patience, and you wait while the food gets divided by the mouths until the answer is zero. The assault everyone remembers is the last five minutes of a process that grinds for ten years. Strip away the heroism and every fortress in history collapses into the same three questions: who controls the water, who can outwait whom, and who is willing to do the unspeakable thing first.

This is Social Story Wrestling for the long history of organized stubbornness. 60 cut-and-play cards running 11,000 years, from the first paranoid wall at Jericho to the last refusal at Masada. You do not study the siege. You staff it. Pick up Cassandra, the Battering Ram, or the Impatient King, perform the role out loud, and let the table rule on whether your bit holds or the whole position comes down on your head.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Siege Kompendium Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring Cassandra (100% correct, zero engagement metrics, screaming doom at a crowd that won't look up from its feed), The Great Chain (physical DRM for the ocean, a harbor sealed so tight no fleet gets in), and The Wooden Horse (a piece of theater so audacious nobody thought to check the trunk).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no setup, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and a deck sorted into 15 themed chapters so you can run a single brawl or march the whole campaign from Foundations to Aftermath.
- The Siege Engine: every layer of the machine made playable. Kinetic weapons like the Trebuchet and the Orban Bombard, defensive nastiness from Boiling Water to Hot Sand to the Murder Hole, the slow biology of starvation and plague, the diplomacy of heralds and broken truces, and the quiet endings nobody puts on a statue: the Empty Victory, the Rat, Oblivion.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this once and you stop being a customer, you become a resident of the Kayfabizarro historical line. New chapters, the booster sheets this cycle still owes you, and every future drop in the history series land in your library as free updates. You bought a door, not a box.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I draw siege history as comedy because the heroic version is the real con: the charge gets the mural, the starvation gets edited out, and we keep mistaking the people who built the walls for the people who deserved them. Naming the machinery out loud is how you stop saluting it. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take it, cut it, play it. Want to support the craft? Every coin goes straight back into the ink and the next deck.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"No wall keeps the world out. It only decides who runs out of grain first."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
